document.title: Usama bin Ladin: Charge Reiterates U.S. Concern to Key Taliban Official, Who Sticks to Well-Known Taliban Positions (Islama 09222)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Secret] Wakil Ahmed tells Eastham he discussed U.S. concerns with Mullah Omar and that the Taliban still consider bin Laden innocent. He says the Taliban remain deeply upset over the Khost strikes and calls the U.S. 'murderers of Afghans'.

persons.name: Wakil Ahmed
persons.role: Mullah Omar's senior assistant; high-ranking Taliban leader with close access to Omar

mentions.quote: CHARGE MET DECEMBER 19 WITH MAULAWI WAKIL AHMED, MULLAH OMAR'S SENIOR ASSISTANT.
"THERE ARE THOUSANDS OF BIN LADINS IN THE WORLD."
PERSONALLY DISCUSSED THE U.S. CONCERNS WITH "AMIR-AL-MUMINEEN" (COMMANDER OF THE FAITHFUL) MULLAH OMAR.
OMAR HAD STRESSED THE NEED FOR FURTHER INFORMATION ABOUT THE U.S. CONCERNS.

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
persons.role: Terrorist leader hosted by the Taliban as a 'guest'

mentions.quote: BIN LADIN IS "A GUEST," HE IS NOT ALLOWED INTERVIEWS WITH THE PRESS
HE HAS GIVEN A WRITTEN OATH THAT HE WILL NOT UNDERTAKE TERRORIST ACTIVITIES.
CHARGE MET DECEMBER 19 WITH MAULAWI WAKIL AHMED
IN ISLAMABAD FOR A MEETING WITH VISITING UN SPECIAL ENVOY LAKHDAR BRAHIMI.

persons.name: Jalaluddin Haqqani
persons.role: Taliban figure who met the US Charge earlier in the week and briefed Wakil
persons.status_detail: The document says only 'HAQQANI'; identification with Jalaluddin is inferred.

mentions.quote: WAKIL SAID HE BEEN BRIEFED BY HAQQANI ON THE MEETING EARLIER IN THE WEEK.

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: De facto Afghan authority, hosting bin Ladin; courts exonerated him in late November 1998.

organizations.name: United Nations
organizations.notes: Brahimi visited as UN Special Envoy.

places.name: Islamabad
places.significance: Site of the meeting between the Charge and Wakil Ahmed.

places.name: Kandahar
places.significance: Wakil Ahmed's base; Taliban feared a US attack on it.

places.name: Khost
places.significance: Site of the August 1998 US Tomahawk cruise missile attack on terrorist camps.

key_claims: The Taliban rejected expelling bin Ladin and said they considered him a guest who had given a written oath not to carry out terrorist activities.
Wakil Ahmed demanded concrete evidence or proof of bin Ladin's guilt and claimed the US concerns were an alibi.
A Taliban court exonerated bin Ladin in late November 1998 for lack of evidence.
The Taliban inferred from the US 'three-point' message that the US intended to attack Afghanistan, possibly Kandahar.
Wakil newly emphasized the US Khost missile attack that killed Afghans, calling Americans murderers of Afghans.
The US warned that the standoff fostered a view that the Taliban were bin Ladin's host, protector and collaborator; Wakil denied collaboration.
